parole.significato: Forming the systematic names of alkenes, indicating the presence of a carbon–carbon double bond.
parole.testo: From international chemical terminology, ultimately from Ancient Greek -ηνή (-ēnḗ, “feminine suffix denoting origin”), the feminine form of -ηνός (-ēnós), from Proto-Indo-European *-nós (“adjective-forming suffix”). Compare Danish -en and Swedish -en (“chemical suffix”).

parole.significato: -logist, -log (a person who studies or is an expert in the related -logy (Norwegian Bokmål: -logi))
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek -λόγος (-lógos, “-logist”), from λέγω (légō, “I arrange; say”), from Proto-Indo-European *leǵ- (“to gather, collect”).

parole.significato: -logy (a branch of learning; a study of a particular subject)
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek -λογία (-logía), from λόγος (lógos, “explanation”) (with the suffix -ῐ́ᾱ (-ĭ́ā, abstract noun suffix), from Proto-Indo-European *-i-eh₂ (creates collective nouns)), from λέγω (légō, “to say, speak”), from Proto-Indo-European *leǵ- (“to gather, collect”).

parole.significato: Used to form nouns denoting subatomic particles, quanta, molecular units, or substances; -on
parole.testo: A new formation from words such as ion (“ion”), from Ancient Greek -ου (-ou), neuter of -ος (-os), from Proto-Indo-European *-os (creates nouns from verb stems).

parole.significato: Used to form nouns denoting chemical compounds; -yl
parole.testo: A new formation from Ancient Greek ὕλη (húlē, “wood, forest; material, matter”), from Proto-Indo-European *swel-, *sel- (“firewood, wood, beam”).
